To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of α-tocopheryl acetate (α-TOC) to vegetable oils and triglycerides, as an effective antioxidant, is dependent on the unsaturation of the fatty acids, and that it has the ability to act as a free radical scavenger.
the antioxidant activity of α-tocpherol depends on its concentration and that the higher the concentration the more efficient it is.

the oxidation of the crude vegetable oils and the fatty acids and triglyceride components of these oils is dependent on their unsatuation and the antioxidant effect is dependent on the amount and the type of α-tocophorol added.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidation of edible oil, triglycerides and fatty acids, as well as the effect of antioxidant addition on the process.
the influence of the unsaturation degree on oxidation of fatty acids and triglyceride and with antioxidant effect of α-tocpherol.
the oxidation process of edible oils and its components (fatty acid and triglyceride).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AT in small amounts inhibited the formation of carbon-centered radicals and in high amounts it accelerated the formation of PBN/AT adducts, which is a consequence of the antioxidant properties of AT.
AT addition has a dual effect, i.e. both pro- and antioxidative effect on the oxidation process of edible oil, fatty acids, and triglycerides, and it depends on the AT concentration.
the addition of α-tocpherol to the edible oils and their derivatives (fatty acids, triglycerides) is a very efficient antioxidant and the efficiency is dependent on the AT amount added.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antioxidant effect of α-tocpherol on edible oils is dependent on their composition, and the antioxidant addition influences the free radicals creation and the stability of the formed carbon-centered radicals.
the α-tocopherols addition in the studied samples led to a decrease in the formation of carbon-centered lipid radicals and an increase in the formation of the PBN/AT adducts.
the addition of AT as a radical scavenger is a promising way to improve the stability of edible oil and its components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
α-tocopherols are effective antioxidants and their addition to edible oils and their components can improve the stability of these oils.
the addition of AT to edible oils, fatty acids and triglyceride samples can be used to control oxidation processes.
α-tocopherols have the ability to inhibit lipid peroxidation in edible oils and their components.
